linkedin.title: Most news apps are built to keep you scrolling, not to keep you informed.
linkedin.body:
We have all been there. You read a headline, scan a few paragraphs, and feel like you know the story. But five minutes later, you realize you missed the context. You know what happened, but you do not know why it matters or how we got here.

That is exactly why we built Deep Dive Mode at Headlinne. We wanted to move beyond the surface level.

Deep Dive Mode does not just summarize the news. It connects the dots. It pulls in relevant history, explains the key players, and highlights the broader implications of a single event. It turns a quick update into a complete picture.

The goal is simple. We want to help you understand the story, not just consume the words. When you have the full context, you can form your own opinions instead of just reacting to the latest alert.

I believe we need more clarity in our news feeds, not just more noise. This is our attempt to fix that.

reels.title: The Solar System chose fire over ice from the very beginning
reels.hook: The Solar System chose fire over ice from the very beginning

beats.caption: The Solar System chose fire over ice from the very beginning
Here is how our solar system built its first solid planets.
beats.detail: It started with heat, not ice.
beats.narration: Here is how our solar system built its first solid planets from the very beginning.

beats.caption: Ancient iron meteorites show the system chose fire over ice.
beats.detail: Iron space rocks hold the secret.
beats.narration: Ancient iron meteorites reveal that the early solar system chose fire over ice.

beats.caption: Early building blocks were heat-forged beads instead of water-rich dust.
beats.detail: A clear divide in cosmic ingredients.
beats.narration: The raw materials were heat-forged rock beads, effectively excluding most water-rich dust.

beats.caption: This selective process happened within the first million years.
beats.detail: It was a very fast start.
beats.narration: This selective process happened incredibly quickly, within just the first million years of existence.

beats.caption: This means early bodies were built from hot, dry rock.
beats.narration: So, the first solid bodies were constructed almost entirely from that hot, dry rock.

beats.caption: Understanding this changes how we view planetary formation.
beats.detail: We are rewriting the early history.
beats.narration: Understanding this changes how we view the formation of our entire planetary neighborhood.

story_card.headline: Meta is building glasses without cameras
story_card.standfirst: The company is pivoting its AI hardware strategy to focus on lighter, longer-lasting

steps.label: What happened
steps.text: Meta is developing a new version of its smart glasses that will not include a camera.

steps.label: How we got here
steps.text: The company is moving away from camera-heavy hardware to prioritize comfort and battery life.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.text: These glasses will be lighter and offer up to 12 hours of battery life per charge.

steps.label: What to watch
steps.text: Keep an eye on how users react to AI glasses that prioritize long usage over visual recording.

story_card.caption:
Meta is working on new AI glasses that ditch the camera to focus on battery life and weight.

By removing the camera, Meta aims to create a more comfortable device that can last all day. This shift suggests the company is betting on voice and AI assistance over visual capture.

Would you wear smart glasses if they couldn't take photos?
